# self-update: plannotator: the binary download shows no progress

Make `self-update plannotator` show how the download of a new Plannotator release goes. **Motivation:** `plannotator update` runs the upstream `install.sh`, which fetches a binary of about 170 MB with `curl -fsSL`. On a slow route to GitHub the run then prints `Installing v0.28.48.` and nothing else for half an hour, so there is no telling whether it hangs or how much is left:

```
$ self-update plannotator
Plannotator 0.28.48 is available (you have 0.28.44).
Installing v0.28.48.
(nothing for 25 minutes; 83 of 173 MB fetched at ~60 KB/s)
```

The rest of the installer already reports its steps to the terminal; only the download is silent, and the flag that silences it lives in a script fetched afresh on every update.

Expected: when a newer release exists, the download shows its progress (size, speed, time left) and the steps of the installer are printed as they happen; when Plannotator is up to date, the step says so quickly, as now. The script is adapted at a single known place, and that place is asserted: when upstream changes it, or anything else does not fit what self-update relies on, the step says why and falls back to the stock `plannotator update`, so an update is never lost to the adaptation. An update already running elsewhere is not started a second time.

Out of scope: speeding up the download itself or the route to GitHub; asking upstream for a progress option; the background auto-update of Plannotator.
